entries.title: FDA recall data expose distinct firm-notice, FDA-posting, classification and revision clocks
entries.decision: Official FDA API documentation distinguishes recallinitiationdt (firm first notified the public/consignees), postedinternetdt (first FDA Enforcement Report posting, blank for some older records before 2022-10-25), centerclassificationdt (later hazard classification), enforcementreportdt (weekly report date) and eventlmd (last modification). FDA's field history is tracked for recalls posted or updated since 2018-07-24, and the agency notes that voluntary firm warnings often predate FDA classification. This is a potential clock-decomposition lead for the already documented FDA frontier, not a new candidate or a market-return hypothesis.
entries.next_action: Keep this in reserve. If the existing FDA frontier is selected later, use a fixed outcome-blind coverage sample, preserve dated original notices/weekly report vintages and field-level revision history, and keep unknown first-public clocks unknown. Do not expand active focus or assign a runner.

Reconsider only when an approved, frozen workpack has a measured Windows-specific bottleneck and a dedicated isolated label such as trading-agent-research-d can route only approved work. Prefer a dedicated isolated/ephemeral environment over a persistent runner on a credential-bearing work PC.

entries.title: Separate actual running jobs from queued jobs and make next gates receipt-driven

A pending Q220 population-repair run was also visible while the Q220 55-record compiler+independent PIT chain was already positive. The correction builds the queue from the current receipt-backed pipeline, tracks job-level status separately from parent workflow status, displays waiting runs without calling them active work, removes stale workflow/runner/ETA routes for unapproved workpacks and keeps an active Q104 census single-flight.

entries.title: Recent 2026 work supports strict value, source-vintage and model-vintage lineage
entries.decision: Reviewed three recent methods papers: Wang's PIT data integrity framework (SSRN 7183438), Lyle/Siano/Yohn's re-adjusted financial statement data study (SSRN 5107985, revised 2026), and Chen et al. on future-trained time-series models (arXiv 2609.20554). These are preprints/working papers, not candidate evidence. The actionable shared point is that source values, public-time basis, transformation/version lineage and any future learned representation's training cutoff must not be collapsed into a single date or latest-value record.
entries.next_action: Keep Q104:I19, Q220 and Q221 as the only active focus. For Q220 preserve as-filed versions and representation mapping; for Q221 do not promote policy-vintage evidence into award-level public-clock proof. Do not use AI outputs as scientific evidence or expand active dispatch.
